module purpose: neorv32_onewire is a bus-controlled 1-Wire controller. It stores enable and timing settings, queues transmit commands into a TX FIFO, generates timed 1-Wire output and input sampling, writes received data and presence results into an RX FIFO, returns status/data on the bus response port, exports a clock-generator enable, and raises an interrupt when enabled and idle with an empty TX queue.

use-case flows.value: control settings written into the controller: enable, clear request, clock prescaler, and clock divider
10-bit transmit command/data word queued into the TX FIFO
configured clock source and divider generate serial timing ticks
serial engine executes queued commands, drives onewire_o, samples onewire_i, and forms the RX result word
interrupt event when the controller is enabled, the TX FIFO is empty, and no transfer is active
control/status bits and RX FIFO result word returned on bus reads
control, interrupt, clock-generator, serial-engine, and onewire_o state forced to reset values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.enable from the bus write at line 142, and that state then controls FIFO clearing when disabled (lines 199 and 231), clock generation (lines 258 and 263), serial activation (line 311), interrupt generation (line 243), and the external clock-generator enable output at line 273; it is also read back at line 150. Corrupting this state changes whether the block runs or is force-cleared, so both operate and report flows depend on its integrity and availability.

The control write stores ctrl.clear at line 143, line 140 forces it back to 0 each cycle, and lines 199 and 231 use it to assert the TX and RX FIFO clear controls wired to the FIFO sub-units at lines 186 and 218. Integrity matters because an incorrect clear loses queued transfers or leaves stale receive data in the start and read-out flows; availability matters because a requested flush must reach both FIFOs.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial bit-time configuration and tick generation
conceptual assets.reasoning: Control writes at lines 144 and 145 store the prescaler and divider, and the clock generator uses them at lines 260 to 265 to select a clkgen_i source, count with clk_cnt, and raise clk_tick. The serial engine then uses clk_tick or clk_tick2 at lines 329, 346, 360, 366, and 374 to launch slots and sample the wire. Integrity of 1-Wire timing depends on preserving these settings and the generated tick/count state; availability depends on producing ticks whenever the block is enabled and the selected source pulses.

conceptual assets.concept: Active 1-Wire transaction state, payload, and driven line level
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow forms fifo.tx_wdata at line 201 and enqueues it at line 200. During execution, serial.state leaves idle when TX data is available (lines 317 and 318), command bits choose the transfer kind and bit count (lines 323 to 335), serial.sreg loads the transfer byte at line 328, serial.tick_cnt advances on timing ticks (lines 361 and 367), serial.busy is derived at line 394, and onewire_o is driven by the state-machine decisions at lines 299 to 302. Integrity of the actual transfer depends on preserving this queued value and progression state; availability depends on advancing from queued work to completion at lines 355 and 379.

The external wire input enters at onewire_i and is synchronized into serial.wire_in at line 296. Read slots capture serial.sample from that synchronized input at lines 346 and 347 and shift it into serial.sreg at lines 350 to 352, while reset slots capture serial.presence at lines 374 and 375. Line 232 packs serial.presence and serial.sreg into fifo.rx_wdata, line 233 writes the RX FIFO, and software later reads that result at lines 161 and 162. Integrity requires the queued result word to match the sampled wire values; availability depends on writing the result on completion.

The report flow registers irq_o from ctrl.enable, not fifo.tx_avail, and not serial.busy at line 243, with reset to 0 at line 241. External logic depends on receiving this event only for that exact enabled, idle, TX-empty condition, and availability depends on producing the event whenever the condition holds on a clock edge.
